The experience concludes with a short sightseeing walk through Estelí and some free time.

The tour begins in Vidigal, on the slopes of Two Brothers Mountain. A motorcycle taxi takes you to the upper part of the neighborhood, where you continue on foot through tropical forest.

The trail leads toward the summit of Two Brothers Mountain, approximately 400 meters high. Viewpoints along the way reveal Lagoa, Ipanema, Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado, Pedra da Gávea, and Rocinha.

After descending, you will walk through Vidigal's streets. Your guide will explain the history of the favelas and contemporary urban life. The excursion ends with a drive through Rocinha and a return to your hotel.

## Coffee Valley and Its Fazendas

Coffee Valley preserves the history of 19th-century Brazil, when coffee plantations generated enormous wealth and estates and towns grew around them. Fazendas, or rural estates, remain among the green hills, offering a glimpse into plantation owners' lives and how their properties were run. Their architecture tells the story of the past through windows, verandas, and the layout of the buildings.

This journey is as much about the estates themselves as the landscapes between them. Beyond the urban sprawl lies another side of Brazil: low hills, roadside trees, and homes connected to the history of coffee. The region appeals to travelers who enjoy discovering a country through everyday life and its rural heritage. Specific fazendas are selected as part of the agreed itinerary.

The excursion lasts 7–8 hours. Transportation, a guide, and dinner are included. Additional activities are charged separately. There is time to take in the details: examine an old facade, listen to stories about how the estates operated, and simply enjoy the valley views.

The Fiesta Gaucho excursion takes place on a ranch approximately 80 km from Buenos Aires and introduces the life and traditions of Argentine gauchos. They once led a nomadic lifestyle, and many later took up farming and cattle ranching.

Today's gauchos demonstrate their horseback riding skills and their use of lassos, knives, and boleadoras. Boleadoras consist of three stones tied together by cords and were traditionally used to catch and immobilize cattle.

The program features folk dancing and a traditional Argentine lunch. The excursion lasts approximately 8 hours.
